widgetMetadata.instructions: Each entry under `widgets` describes one chart/widget rendered on this page of the Israeli Ecosystem dashboard. Descriptions are result-agnostic: they explain what the visualization shows and how to interpret it, not the specific numbers. The `dataPaths` array on each entry lists dot-notation paths inside this same JSON file where the underlying data for that widget lives (e.g. "kpis.patentingStartups" or "ipIntensity.items") When summarizing or answering questions about a number from this snapshot, locate the relevant widget(s) by `dataPaths` and quote the corresponding `description` to explain the metric. Widgets that have a 10 year trend usually show the total overall (across all years) and you get the exact data for each year in the past 10 years. The 10 year data do not add up to the total of course

startups:map.title: Israel Startup Map
startups:map.description: Geographic distribution of Israeli startups by their registered address in Israel. Each city marker is sized by the number of startups with an active legal registration in that city and colored by its administrative district. The legend lists the same totals by district. Only startups with a known registered Israeli address appear.

startups:kpi-total-startups.title: Total Startups
startups:kpi-total-startups.description: Total number of Israeli startups in the dataset (active, exited, and closed combined). The bar chart shows new startups by founding year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-funding-rounds.title: Funding Rounds
startups:kpi-funding-rounds.description: Total number of equity rounds raised by Israeli startups across all time: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the count of rounds closed each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-total-raised.title: Total Raised
startups:kpi-total-raised.description: Total capital (USD) Israeli startups raised in equity rounds: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the dollar amount raised each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-acquisitions.title: Acquisitions
startups:kpi-acquisitions.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via a completed acquisition, meaning a deal that actually went ahead. The bar chart shows acquisitions by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-ipos.title: IPOs
startups:kpi-ipos.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via IPO and reached the market, meaning shares priced or trading on a public exchange. The bar chart shows IPOs by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-time-to-exit.title: Time to Exit
startups:kpi-time-to-exit.description: Average number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, capped at 30+ years.

startups:survival-distribution.title: Survival Distribution
startups:survival-distribution.description: Breakdown of all Israeli startups by current status: Active (still operating), Closed (shut down or dissolved), and Exit (acquired or went public). The center of the donut shows the total number of startups, or the value of the hovered slice.

startups:exit-funnel.title: Exit Funnel
startups:exit-funnel.description: How many Israeli startups make it through each progressive milestone toward an exit: All startups (everyone in the dataset), Funded (raised at least one equity round), $1M+ (raised at least $1 million in total), $10M+ (raised at least $10 million in total), Exit (a completed acquisition or public listing). The percentage on each segment is the retention from the All-startups stage.

startups:time-to-exit.title: Time To Exit
startups:time-to-exit.description: Average and median number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram below shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, with the rightmost bucket capturing every exit at 30 or more years.

startups:industry-mix.title: Industry Share Over Time
startups:industry-mix.description: Stacked bar chart of the industry mix of Israeli startups by founding year. Each bar is one year, broken into 6 industry categories (IT and Telecom, Healthcare and Food, Consumer Goods and Services, Energy and Utilities, Financial Services, Media and Entertainment). Sub-industries that fall outside these 6 are bucketed into Unknown and excluded from the visible mix. The legend on the right shows each industry overall total and share across all years.

startups:signal-deeptech.title: Deeptech
startups:signal-deeptech.description: Share of Israeli startups flagged as deeptech. Deep tech companies require significant resources, long development cycles, specialized expertise, and substantial investment. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of deeptech startups.

startups:signal-global.title: Operating Globally
startups:signal-global.description: Share of Israeli startups that have a product with a global audience. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of globally operating startups.

startups:trending-up.title: Sub-Industries Trending Up By Share Of Total
startups:trending-up.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has grown the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:trending-down.title: Sub-Industries Trending Down By Share Of Total
startups:trending-down.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has shrunk the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:feed-funding.title: Funding Feed
startups:feed-funding.description: Latest funding rounds added to the dataset, gathered from multiple verifiable sources. Unlike the headline funding figures, this feed carries every round type, grants and venture debt included, each one flagged with isNonEquity so you can tell them apart.

startups:feed-new-startups.title: New Startups
startups:feed-new-startups.description: Latest startups added to the dataset. Not necessarily new Startups founded.

startups:feed-notable.title: Notable Events
startups:feed-notable.description: Latest notable events gathered form news feeds, including acquisitions, IPOs, corporate events, strategic partnerships and more.

newStartups.description: Cortex Analytix is an AI research company based in Israel. Its team of scientists, engineers and machine learning experts works to advance the state of the art in artificial intelligence, building novel computer systems that learn to solve difficult problems on their own.
Aerospace engineering and technology firm specializing in the development and certification of innovative aerospace equipment and systems for the aviation sector.
newStartups.businessModel: B2B manufacturing and certification of aerospace components

newStartups.description: AI-powered career management platform that optimizes resumes, tracks job applications, and provides interview preparation for job seekers.

Sci-Co is an independent community platform that promotes collaborations between academia and industry. It connects academic researchers and entrepreneurs through events, knowledge sharing, and mentorship, providing tools to bridge the gap between the academic and business worlds.

Cubic-C provided services enabling the execution of secure e-commerce and e-banking transactions via common mobile phone handsets. Its proprietary platform integrated consumers, e-tailers, merchants, cellular network operators, clearing houses, banks and credit card companies, turning existing mobile phones into secure e-payment transaction terminals. The system was beta-tested and initiated pilots with leading banks and mobile phone service providers in Europe and the Far East. The company ceased to operate in Q1 2007.
Cloud-based HR and workforce management platform for the restaurant industry, offering location-based time tracking, shift scheduling, payroll, and invoicing.

GLOS is a digital marketplace and SaaS platform for the beauty and wellness industry. It lets customers compare and book services, helping them find suitable service providers while saving time. For businesses, it builds efficient sales channels through optimized marketing, reduced expenses, and insights for growth opportunities.
Medical device company developing a real-time intra-operative cancer detection system used during surgery to improve patient outcomes.

WebFortify provides web application penetration testing services, combining automated and manual techniques to identify security vulnerabilities in clients' online assets. The company offers customized security assessments and detailed reports to help businesses strengthen their web defenses.

SCerise is a pre-market Israeli medical device company developing a non-surgical solution to improve the quality of life of spinal cord injury survivors. The company focuses on research, design and development of its technology in the health tech and life sciences sector.
Machine-learning-based recommender systems provider helping retailers boost sales through personalized product recommendations, similar-product suggestions, and popular-product lists.

Multimodal travel search and booking platform that aggregates multiple transportation providers including railways, airlines, buses, and car-sharing services to offer users a single interface for comparing and booking journeys.
Developer of real-time AI personas designed to interact with humans naturally, focusing on humanizing technology.
E-learning platform providing simplified microbiology laboratory equipment and digital guidance, enabling school students to conduct experiments in the classroom.
Israeli company offering services in the digital field.

Provider of web-based project management and quality control software for construction, paving, and infrastructure projects, offering field reporting, GIS integration, and business intelligence analytics.

Software that restricts non-essential smart device functions to block distracting apps, improving focus and productivity for educational, fleet, and office environments, with mobile security features for corporate information.
SimplyCoach is a management software for sports organizations, offering a digital tool to handle administrative tasks, monitor students, and manage coaching sessions.
A one-stop solution for renewable engineering projects. Specializes in Photovoltaic and Storage systems.
bwise is an embedded software company based in Herzliya, Israel, leading the architecture, design, and development of all software aspects of its products.

notable.summary: Chairman of the Board Bob Marshall and Directors Mike Swinford and William Sigsbee stepped down from the board, effective August 13, 2026.
Chief Financial Officer Almog Adar decided to depart, effective September 30, 2026.
Acquired Benmax's fabrication, design and projects businesses for A$300 million, bringing HyperCube AI Factory manufacturing in-house.
Aidoc's CARE Body CT Multi-Triage solution received eligibility for Medicare New Technology Add-on Payment (NTAP).

Published new data showing US impersonation scam attempts surged 130% in a year, and stating that impersonation scams have more than doubled as Wall Street faces targeted attacks and turnkey scam kits lower barriers for fraud.
Expanded partnership with Yahoo DSP, introducing a creative trafficking API and audience-driven creative decisioning.
Expanded Shopify Managed Markets Version 2.0 to Canada and the UK, the first availability beyond the US, and migrated the remaining merchants from Version 1.0 to Version 2.0.

Acquired by DB Group Investments (49% equity stake). DB Group Investments, a Dubai-based venture capital and investment group, acquired a 49% stake in Blueye AI to support the company's product development and commercial growth. Blueye AI will continue to operate independently under CEO Natali Yaacbson.
Twelve U.S. health systems and Aidoc announced a collaborative initiative to confront America's diagnostic capacity crisis, uniting to enhance diagnostic access and efficiency through clinical AI.
Activated Weill Cornell Medicine and NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell Medical Center as clinical sites in the EASE IDE trial, with the first study procedure completed by Dr. Reem Sharaiha.
AITECH Cloud Network and Secret Network, developed by SCRT Labs, announced a strategic partnership to bring confidential computing and AI to Agent Forge.
Included in CNBC's 2026 list of the World's Top Fintech Companies, recognizing HoneyBook as a leading fintech company for independent businesses.
Appointed Eran Kuratz as Head of Supply Chain and Business Process Administration at subsidiary Scinai Biopharma Services Ltd.

Doral Group signed a $400 million common equity investment in its US subsidiary Doral Renewables LLC, increasing its ownership stake; Clean Air Generation LLC, owned by Doral Renewables CEO Nick Cohen, exchanged its membership interests for cash and Doral Group stock.
Corma launched its defensive cybersecurity AI foundation model and agents, with deployments at Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 companies.
Nanox.AI optimized its medical imaging AI application framework for Intel Core Ultra processors using OpenVINO.

Emerged from stealth at DAC 2026, launching its next-generation SystemVerilog simulator for chip design verification built from the ground up, with a patent-pending engine designed to accelerate full-chip simulation.
Varonis announced it will present at an upcoming investor conference.
Became MongoDB's only authorized professional services delivery partner in Israel.
Deepened its collaboration/ties with Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its growth accelerates.
